How to Write an Opinion Paragraph
An opinion paragraph states a viewpoint and then provides specific examples to support that view.
You structure an opinion paragraph by clearly stating your opinion at the beginning of the paragraph.
Then,  support your opinion with reasons, examples or facts.
Your response must be clear and organized.
Use a  concluding sentence or two, to summarize your argument and restate your opinion.
Adding modals to your opinion paragraph can make your paragraph more persuasive.

Words like therefore, because, since and so can connect ideas.
For example:
There is a connection between second-hand smoke and lung cancer, therefore, public areas should be smoke free.
Smoking in public areas should be banned because we all have a right to clear air.
Since we live in a global community, we need to maintain a healthy environment for anyone.
The medical facts are clear so there should not be any reason to argue against the proposal.
Our lungs should not be polluted for the sake of catering to someone's selfishness .
Shouldn't we as a society, have the collective right to breathe clean air, regardless of location?
We, as a community must take a stand and pressure our elected officials to restrict smoking in all public places.
Writing Tip: Using Modals in Opinion Paragraphs

You can use a variety of modals in your writing to express the different degrees of certainty,  modality of your opinions or arguments. It is important to be as clear as you can, when you discuss your views on a particular subject. It is important to try and be as clear as you can when you discuss your views on a particular subject.
Refer to the chart for a summary of modals you can use in your writing, and an example of how to structure your sentences using the modals. (Punctuation is important.)

images.text: Smoking is a hazardous, destructive habit that should not be allowed in public places. Firstly, it is well-documented that smoking leads to a significant number of health-related issues. Cigarettes contain toxic carcinogens that are directly linked to cancer. Why should we be encouraging people to smoke in the first place when it is costing taxpayers millions of dollars each year in medical bills? Also, studies have also shown that second-hand smoke is extremely harmful. Our lungs should not be polluted for the sake of catering to someone's selfishness .

Secondly, public spaces are exactly that - places meant for everyone. That being the case, to deliberately cloud the air frequented by the non-smoking public with poisonous emissions is simply wrong. I think the rights of non-smoking citizens ought to take precedence over a few stick puffers. People should have the right to go to malls, restaurants, coffee shops, book stores, and not have to worry about ending up fighting lung cancer. Shouldn't we as a society, have the collective right to breathe clean air, regardless of location?

Finally, smokers have a responsibility to the environment. Pollution is a major concern facing our planet. Smokers do nothing to decrease our negative impact on our surroundings. In fact, cigarette butts often litter public areas and are caught in the drains leading to our waterways. I firmly believe that their reckless, deleterious behavior affects everyone and is counter productive in our fight against global warming. We, as a community must take a stand and pressure our elected officials to restrict smoking in all public places. For those smokers who may believe it is their right to smoke; I would say yes, you do. Smokers ought to quit, stay home or use a nicotine patch.  It's as simple as that!
